title: Endpaper ISBN conformance cases
description: The shape of conformance/cases/isbn.json. Every runner validates the case file against this before running a single case, so a file that has drifted from the format fails rather than silently running fewer cases than it looks like it has.

$schema.description: Relative path to this file, so an editor can find it.

domain.description: Which rule set these cases specify. One domain per file.

operation.description: The operation under test. Every implementation maps these names onto its own spelling in an explicit table, so neither language's naming wins.

id.description: Unique within the file. Uniqueness is asserted by the runners: JSON Schema cannot express it across array items.

why.description: Why this case is in the file. A measurement or a rule, never an opinion. The minimum length is there because an empty why passes a presence check and says nothing.

allOf.description: normalise, is-valid-isbn10, is-valid-isbn13 and isbn10-to-isbn13 take a string. Only parse and is-valid are null safe on both sides.
The three predicates answer a boolean and nothing else.
normalise and isbn10-to-isbn13 are total on a string and always answer a string.
parse answers the canonical ISBN-13 or nothing. Never a boolean: is-valid is the predicate.
